capabilities: Sign in to a Garmin account and sync health, performance and activity data into JSON files in the vault
Browse Garmin-style dashboard pages for home, activities, health stats and performance stats
Embed Garmin cards, charts and activity route maps in notes via code blocks and daily note templates
Share an activity as a styled image or export a note with its map to PDF
Store the session refresh token in Obsidian's Secret Storage without saving the password
extras: Not reviewed by Obsidian staff. Planned but unreleased features include an opt-in AI coach (would need a model API key or Ollama) and customizable layouts. With Obsidian Sync, 'Sync all other types' must be enabled for the data JSON to reach other devices. Detailed setup, troubleshooting and security docs live outside the README.
intentEvidence: I took a lot of its ideas, like file properties on daily notes, but wanted headless sign-in, cross-platform support and data visualisation.
motivation: The author took ideas from Garmin Health Sync but wanted headless sign-in, cross-platform support and data visualisation, and started by working out whether headless authentication was possible.
problem: Garmin's own views are online-only app or web pages; Obsidian users have no way to keep their health data locally, view it offline, or place it in their own notes.

relations.evidence: Garmin Health Sync: the inspiration for the project, and I believe the first Garmin–Obsidian plugin.
an actively maintained Garmin Connect library that saved a huge amount of reverse-engineering work

summary: Syncs Garmin health, performance and activity data into your vault as JSON and renders it in a dashboard and embeddable note cards.
